blockers.title: The RPM branch asserts an archive blob but defines no operation that acquires or passes those exact bytes to rpm
evidence: archiveAcquisition.source is only the noun phrase the unique installed rpm package blob for this NEVRA from rpmdb. It names no rpmdb query, librpm API, repository/index object, pathname, file descriptor, or byte-returning membership rule. The v23 reconstruction grammar was deleted, leaving no producer operation that yields the asserted octets.

The mapped owning-package and header queries return NEVRA and SHA256HEADER metadata, not an archive-byte handle under any rule in this candidate. A system can therefore have the required installed NEVRA/header record and no original .rpm archive selected by the contract; source then yields zero blobs and every such observation refuses.

archiveAcquisition.checksigArgv places <those-exact-archive-bytes> directly in an argv array. The candidate never maps that placeholder to a stable pathname or descriptor. Arbitrary archive octets are not a defined rpm(8) pathname operand, so the specified command cannot demonstrate that rpm checked the byte sequence whose sha-256 was retained.

No before/after identity or held-handle rule binds a materialized file to archiveDigest across rpm --checksig and rpm2cpio. If a producer silently downloads, finds a cache entry, reconstructs, or writes a temporary file, it has introduced the exact source/handle operation that the closed contract omits.

The branch is mandatory for amzn, fedora, rhel, sles, opensuse-leap, and opensuse-tumbleweed PLATFORM-ATTESTED identities. Zero-blob refusal is therefore not merely an optional unsupported-publisher path.
blockers.impact: The v23 SHA256HEADER conflation is removed, but v24 still cannot execute one archive-byte verification chain on its RPM publishers. Conforming producers either blanket-refuse ordinary installed systems or invent different archive sources and file bindings, so G22 cannot reproduce the signed package identity or the manifest used for object joins.
blockers.requiredRepair: Name one real, deterministic archive acquisition for RPM publishers, including the exact repository/database object and selection key, byte-returning API or immutable pathname/descriptor, and zero/ambiguity rules. Hash the acquired handle, validate that same held or revalidated file with rpm/librpm, and feed those exact bytes to rpm2cpio. If materialization is required, specify creation, fsync/identity, no-replacement, and before/after digest checks. Do not represent raw archive bytes as an argv pathname.

blockers.title: The IMA record can authenticate a measured file without binding that file to the currently executing kernel
evidence: entrySelection requires a file-path that is the executing kernel image, but no operation derives or verifies that predicate. runningKernelImagePath is expressly retired, and the new IMA branch supplies no boot identity, kexec lineage, loaded-image handle, PCR/event-log join, or other link from an ima-ng pathname to the code currently executing.

A counterexample survives every specified comparison: boot a different kernel M, retain an authentic package kernel K on disk, and cause K to be measured/appraised so the IMA list contains K's sha-256 and path. The selected digest equals authenticatedKernelMember.sha256 and packagePayloadDigest remains authentic, while M continues executing. The candidate has no check that distinguishes this state from K being the running kernel.

The only acquired evidence is ascii_runtime_measurements constrained to template ima-ng, yet trustRoot alternatively requires appraisal state or a verifiable IMA signature/keyid, and successRecord always requires keyid. No field source, policy parser, appraisal-result record, signature bytes, key lookup, or signature-verification operation supplies that keyid or proves the stated mode from the acquired record.

freshness compares list-entry existence with runPreselectionRecord.observedAt, but observedAt is this contract's logical event counter and is not joined to any IMA record field. No retained list snapshot/digest, TPM quote, boot nonce, held handle, or before/after sequence implements the later-substitution refusal.

measuredRepresentation remains circular prose and does not resolve whether the authenticated package member bytes are the compressed boot artifact, decompressed kernel image, or immutable executing pages. Equality of two sha-256 strings therefore does not close the representation or execution bind.
blockers.impact: A host can present a validly measured and packaged kernel file while another kernel executes, causing a false allow for the mandatory pathless OS-ABI identity. Alternatively, strict producers cannot construct the required keyid/freshness record and blanket-refuse Linux qualification.
blockers.requiredRepair: Use a measurement ceremony that is cryptographically bound to the current boot and exact executing representation. Define the report/event format, measured-boot or runtime interface, PCR/policy and signature validation, trust anchors, boot/run freshness, loaded-image selection, and exact equality to the authenticated package member. If IMA is retained, specify how an IMA event is proven to be the booted kernel rather than any measured file, and use a template/evidence form that actually carries every required trust field.

shouldFix.title: The new archive-member grammar is not wired into the APT manifest or the live file-backed join and has overlapping RPM prefix rules
evidence: archiveMemberPathGrammar.debDataTar appears only in the grammar's own definition. apt-secure.extractAfter still says merely to extract authenticatedManifest from data.tar and never requires debDataTar normalization.

joinMust consumes the older packageRelativePathRule, not archiveMemberPathGrammar.INSTALL-ROOT-VOLUME or .EXTERNAL-ORIGIN. The older rules likewise never say that their result is normalized by the new grammar. Adding a named grammar beside the live join does not make it normative for that join.

rpmCpio says to strip a single leading '.' or './'. Those prefixes overlap: './usr/lib/x' can become '/usr/lib/x' if '.' is stripped or 'usr/lib/x' if './' is stripped. The former then violates noLeadingSlash while the latter passes. The rule gives no longest-prefix precedence and also accidentally reaches ordinary dot-prefixed member names.

The reject list names '.' and '..' without saying whether rejection applies to the whole path or every component, so a producer can disagree on names such as a/../b even before the disconnected INSTALL/EXTERNAL transform is considered.

authenticatedManifest still rejects any repeated sha256 even though joinMust now selects by both canonical path and hash; two different paths with identical regular-file bytes are needlessly ambiguous only because the old hash-only uniqueness rule survived.
shouldFix.impact: The explicit same-member equality repairs the v23 false allow, but RPM, APT, and opened-path producers can still derive different relativePath bytes or refuse the same archive. The path half of the retained equality is not one reproducible cross-publisher serialization.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make archiveMemberPathGrammar the sole normative input to authenticatedManifest and packageRelativePathRule. Explicitly require apt extraction to use debDataTar and both INSTALL/EXTERNAL transforms to use the same grammar. Define component-wise rejection and one unambiguous longest-prefix strip (normally './' only) that preserves lawful dot-prefixed names. Require unique canonical paths/entries; do not require hash uniqueness once path+hash selects the member.

shouldFix.title: The separated RPM header identity is called retained but has no retained field, while digestSuccess has no producer operation
evidence: headerIdentity.role says SHA256HEADER is retained rpm header identity, but headerIdentity occurs only in this operation definition. It is absent from the closed package-db trustDecision, authenticityCore, all objectAuthenticityBind variants, and retainedEventSchema; no event can serialize the promised retained value.

The v23 digestArgv was deleted, but its sibling digestSuccess rule remains. No rule says whether digestSuccess validates archiveDigest, headerIdentity.queryArgv, or another command, so the live operation contains an orphaned success parser.
headerIdentity.queryArgv has no directly attached success/output grammar. Treating the unrelated digestSuccess as its parser is an inference, not a closed reference.

The role says SHA256HEADER MUST NOT equal authenticityCore.payload.digest. Separation of semantic roles should prohibit using or equating the fields, not require their 256-bit values to be unequal; an accidental equality would be refused for no authenticity reason.
shouldFix.impact: After the archive source is repaired, implementations can still retain incompatible RPM evidence or omit a value the operation calls mandatory retained identity. The closed trace cannot reproduce which header query succeeded.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Either remove SHA256HEADER entirely if it is not load-bearing, or add one closed retained field with its exact 64-hex output grammar and bind it to headerIdentity.queryArgv. Delete or explicitly attach digestSuccess. Replace value-level MUST NOT equal with MUST NOT be used as, derived as, or substituted for the signed archive digest.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 2 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. v24 adds the missing same-member equalities, fixes association-token placement and stale build-id text, separates SHA256HEADER from the signed archive digest, and serializes the macOS same-guest record. It still does not acquire or address one executable RPM archive, and its IMA event can describe an authentic file without proving that file is the running kernel. The new member-path grammar is not fully connected, and RPM header evidence remains outside the closed trace. DR-126 remains OPEN; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, G22 qualification, sealing, application, or implementation authority is created.
